props.markdown: Go through the marks, turn the cards and answer the question: then you may go on.

items.title: Isobars
items.markdown: Lines of equal pressure. Close together, they mean strong wind.

items.title: Fronts
items.markdown:
Where two air masses meet. A cold front brings showers and a sudden change of wind; a warm front brings low clouds and steady rain for hours.

On the chart, triangles mark a cold front and half-circles a warm one: they point the way the front moves, so the weather they carry comes from that side.

A front that stops moving is drawn with both marks, on either side of the line.

items.title: Pressure
items.markdown: The figure at the centre of a low or a high, in hectopascals.

cards.title: Warm front
cards.markdown: Low clouds and steady rain for hours, then milder air. The rain can last half a day before the sky lifts, and the wind turns as the front passes: climbs wait until it has.

items.title: Why hectopascals?
items.markdown: One hectopascal is one millibar: older charts used millibars.

props.stem: Which front brings steady rain for hours?

options.feedback: Yes: low clouds and steady rain.
A cold front brings showers, then a clear sky.
A ridge is high pressure: settled weather.

props.markdown: You can read a chart: check it every morning before you climb.
